source: (2025) Cognitive Workspace: Active Memory Management for LLMs
finding: Paper explicitly invokes the Clark and Chalmers Otto notebook and builds an active, agent-managed external memory. Reports high reuse of stored items versus passive RAG.
numbers: Memory reuse 54.52% (4 rounds), 57.1% (10 rounds) vs 0% for RAG. Net efficiency gain 17-18% after counting 3.3x more operations. Working memory size shrank 4 to 3 items.
limits: Reuse of stored items is a bookkeeping metric, not answer accuracy. No human comparison. Author-defined baseline gets 0% by construction.
agent_relevance: Treat notes as an active workspace the agent edits, not a passive store; track reuse rate as a cheap diagnostic.

source: (2025) Cognitive Workspace: Active Memory Management for LLMs
finding: Statistics in this paper look implausible, so the claim should be treated as weak.
numbers: Reported Cohen's d = 195.66, t(18) = 69.60, p < 0.001; operation ratio CW/RAG 3.31; break-even at round 6.
limits: A d near 200 suggests deterministic or simulated runs with tiny variance. Net efficiency is a derived ratio (reuse/(1+extra ops)). Do not cite as strong evidence.
agent_relevance: Do not adopt the headline gain without a replication on real tasks with accuracy as the outcome.

source: Klett and Ahle (2024) Extended Mind Transformers
finding: Gives the model a bank of stored memories retrieved by its own attention keys in most decoder layers; no fine-tuning. Named after the extended mind idea.
numbers: Counterfactual long-range retrieval benchmark, accuracy at 2k/4k/8k/16k tokens: Extended Mind Llama2-7b 38.59/37.95/36.00/33.54%; plain Chat Llama2 42.74/41.96/33.50/17.68%.
limits: The extended model is worse at short length (2k) and much better at 16k. Counterfactual facts only, so it tests use of context, not knowledge. Preprint.
agent_relevance: External store helps most when the problem exceeds the internal window; at short length extra machinery can cost accuracy.

source: Klett and Ahle (2024) Extended Mind Transformers
finding: Combined with RAG, the extended-memory model beat GPT-4 on the same benchmark.
numbers: Extended Mind Chat Llama2-70b + RAG 59.34/53.13/53.00/50.00% vs Chat Llama2-70b + RAG 50.21/47.32/44.50/45.12% vs GPT-4 52.28/50.00/46.00/43.29%. Authors claim +6% on average over SoTA.
limits: Authors' own new benchmark. Retrieval needed in a majority of decoder layers, not just the last ones.
agent_relevance: Retrieval should be driven by the thinker's own state, not only by an outside embedding search.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: Model manages its own paged memory (main context vs archival storage) through function calls. Large gain on recalling facts from old sessions.
numbers: Deep memory retrieval accuracy: GPT-3.5 38.7% to 66.9%; GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%; GPT-4 Turbo 35.3% to 93.4% with MemGPT.
limits: New task made by the authors; LLM-judged. Fixed-context baselines cannot see old sessions, so the gain is partly by design.
agent_relevance: Self-managed external memory is a strong default for long-run agents; log every read and write.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: On nested key-value lookup, plain models collapse while the memory-using agent does not, because it can repeat lookups.
numbers: GPT-3.5 0% at 1 nesting level; GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo 0% by 3 levels; MemGPT with GPT-4 unaffected by nesting depth. GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-3.5 versions still dropped at 2 levels from too few lookups.
limits: Synthetic task. Failure mode of the weaker agent was too few lookups, not wrong lookups.
agent_relevance: Iterated lookup into an external store lets depth grow; the loop must allow enough lookups.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: Each agent keeps an external memory stream with retrieval, reflection and planning. Removing these parts lowers believability in a human ranking study.
numbers: TrueSkill mu: full architecture 29.89; no reflection 26.88; no reflection or planning 25.64; human crowdworker condition 22.95; no memory, planning or reflection 21.21. 100 Prolific raters.
limits: Believability is rated by people and is not task accuracy. One sandbox world.
agent_relevance: Memory stream plus reflection is a measured, additive gain; keep reflection tied to stored records.

source: Yao et al. (2023) ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
finding: Interleaving thoughts with actions on an outside world (search, game) beat acting alone and beat trained imitation and RL agents, using one or two prompt examples.
numbers: ALFWorld best ReAct trial 71% vs best Act 45% vs BUTLER 37%; worst ReAct trial 48% beat both. Abstract: +34% (ALFWorld) and +10% (WebShop) absolute over IL/RL.
limits: Best-of-6 trial selection. On HotpotQA, ReAct alone did not clearly beat chain-of-thought; best results came from combining ReAct with CoT-SC (table layout garbled in extraction, exact cells not recorded).
agent_relevance: Reasoning that reads from and writes to the world is better than reasoning alone; the environment acts as working memory.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Agent stores written self-reflections as episodic memory across trials. Gains on coding, search QA and household tasks.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80.1%. Abstract: +22% on ALFWorld (12 steps), +20% HotpotQA, +11% HumanEval over baselines.
limits: Leetcode Hard was lower than GPT-4 in its table (77.1 vs 80.1). Needs a usable success signal; HumanEval pass@1 uses test feedback.
agent_relevance: Written notes across attempts work only with a real success or failure signal, matching guardrail G2.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Ablation on 100 HotPotQA questions separates plain episodic memory from reflection.
numbers: Self-reflection gave an 8% absolute boost over episodic-memory-only (most recent trajectory).
limits: Only 100 questions; a single task type.
agent_relevance: Store the explanation of why it failed, not only the failed trajectory.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
finding: Code skill library is an external, growing, reusable procedural memory. Strong exploration versus ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT.
numbers: 63 unique items in 160 iterations, 3.3x more than baselines; wooden tool level reached 15.3x faster.
limits: Minecraft only; GPT-4 required (GPT-3.5 variant much worse).
agent_relevance: Executable code stored as skills is an artifact the agent extends; test reuse against a no-library arm.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
finding: Ablations show which external parts matter.
numbers: Random curriculum cut discovered items by 93%. Without the skill library the agent plateaus in later stages.
limits: Three runs per condition.
agent_relevance: A persistent skill store matters most late in a run, not early.

source: Schick et al. (2023) Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
finding: A 6.7B model taught to call a QA tool, calculator, search and calendar lifts zero-shot facts and arithmetic.
numbers: LAMA (SQuAD/GoogleRE/T-REx): Toolformer 33.8/11.5/53.5 vs GPT-J 17.8/4.9/31.9, GPT-3 175B 26.8/7.0/39.8. Math ASDiv/SVAMP/MAWPS: Toolformer 40.4/29.4/44.0 vs tools-disabled 14.8/6.3/15.0.
limits: Column reading from a garbled text table, row order inferred. At most one call per input.
agent_relevance: A small model plus tools can beat a larger model without tools; fits tools as part of the cognitive system.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation with Language Models
finding: Letting a model write intermediate steps in an external buffer (scratchpad) raises accuracy on multi-step computation, the written-notes case of Otto.
numbers: Polynomial evaluation: direct 8.8% vs scratchpad 20.1% (few-shot, 137B); 31.8% vs 50.7% (fine-tuned 8B). Program execution: 11% vs 26.5% few-shot; 20% vs 41.5% fine-tuned.
limits: Synthetic tasks; few-shot program figure uses a modified accuracy criterion.
agent_relevance: Written intermediate state is the cheapest extended-mind move and doubles accuracy on some tasks.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
finding: Interface design to the tool, not the model, drives results. A custom agent-computer interface beat the bare shell.
numbers: 12.5% pass@1 on SWE-bench and 87.7% on HumanEvalFix. Ablation on 300 SWE-bench Lite items: ACI solves 10.7 points more than a default Linux shell agent.
limits: Developed for GPT-4 Turbo; portability shown to one other model. Gains are interface-specific.
agent_relevance: Situated cognition for agents is mostly interface: short feedback, guardrails, small action sets.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
finding: Specific features each matter: editing guardrails (linting), search commands, concise file views, error feedback after each command.
numbers: Text says linting guardrails and concise feedback help; per-cell numbers in Table 3 not reliably extracted (about 18.0% with linting vs about 10-12% in variants without).
limits: Component numbers read from a garbled table; check the paper before quoting.
agent_relevance: Run a check on every edit; show only a window of the file.

source: Jimenez et al. (2024) SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues
finding: Without an interactive tool loop, retrieval-fed models solve almost nothing on real repository issues.
numbers: Claude 2 with a BM25 retriever resolved 1.96% of issues.
limits: One retrieval setup, 2023 models.
agent_relevance: Baseline showing how much of SWE-agent's 12.5% comes from the tool loop.

source: Xu et al. (2025) A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
finding: Zettelkasten-style linked notes that the agent updates itself beat prior memory systems, most on multi-hop questions.
numbers: LoCoMo and DialSim, six models. Multi-hop F1 at least 2x the baselines; about 1,200 tokens per memory operation vs 16,900 for full context; DialSim F1 3.45 vs LoCoMo 2.55 (+35%) vs MemGPT 1.18.
limits: Gains largest on multi-hop; baselines were already strong on simple fact retrieval and adversarial questions.
agent_relevance: Link notes to each other and update old notes; measure multi-hop, not single-hop recall.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: A fact placed in context is not reliably used; position matters. This limits treating context as extended memory.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo multi-document QA fell by over 20% when the relevant passage was in the middle, to below its closed-book accuracy of 56.1%.
limits: 2023 models; later long-context models may differ.
agent_relevance: Put critical notes at the start or end of the prompt; stored does not mean used.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
finding: Externalized search structure (explicit tree of partial thoughts plus code controlling search) lifts a planning task.
numbers: Game of 24: GPT-4 chain-of-thought 4% vs Tree of Thoughts 74%.
limits: Costs many more calls; task chosen to need search.
agent_relevance: Structure held in program state, as in our code-run schema, beats keeping it in one text stream.

source: Zhou et al. (2026) Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review of Memory, Skills, Protocols and Harness Engineering
finding: Review argues agent progress comes from moving burdens from weights to context to a harness, citing Clark and Chalmers (1998), Kirsh (1995) and Hutchins (1995).
numbers: Qualitative; names memory (state across time), skills (procedures), protocols (interaction) and a harness that unifies them.
limits: Review and framework with no new experiment; the cognitive-artifact framing is the authors' reading.
agent_relevance: Matches our design: code owns state, memory and checks; the model fills slots.
quote: intelligence is no longer localized in the model alone

source: Zhou et al. (2026) Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review of Memory, Skills, Protocols and Harness Engineering
finding: Notes a trade-off between parametric and externalized capability and open problems in evaluation and governance.
numbers: No new numbers.
limits: Survey claims not audited here.
agent_relevance: Test each external piece with an ablation against weights-only, as the papers above do.

source: Smart, Clowes and Clark (2025) Synthese, extended LLM via RAG (Digital Andy)
finding: Philosophical case study: a GPT given retrieval over Andy Clark's writing as an external store, asking if it forms an extended system.
numbers: Not measured; seen only in a search snippet (PDF returned 401).
limits: Not opened; details unverified.
agent_relevance: Clark-Chalmers tests (reliability, accessibility, endorsement) map onto agent notes: only trusted, always-available notes count as part of the thinker.

source: Normal Computing (2023) Supersizing Transformers blog
finding: Blog precursor to Extended Mind Transformers, seen in search; numbers are in the arXiv paper above.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Blog, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Use the arXiv paper instead.

source: Clark (2025) Extending minds with generative AI, Nature Communications
finding: Seen only as a search mention; page needed a login redirect. Not verified.
numbers: None.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Skip unless opened later.
